subject: Mutual Action Plan: operational cadence, acceptance criteria, and owner pledges
messages:
From: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@brightlane.io>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com
Cc: priya.raman@brightlane.io
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — operational cadence and acceptance items

Hi Mateo —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. As discussed, our execs want a concise mutual action plan that maps out milestones, acceptance criteria, and clear owners across Product, Security, and Ops. Can you share a working draft we can review this week?

Key asks from our side:
- Production readiness milestones (staging > pre-prod > prod) with gating criteria
- SLA / latency targets per endpoint for peak hours
- Data retention and audit log handoff steps for Security sign-off
- A suggested 6-week pilot cadence with check-in dates

If you can send a draft MAP and a short proposed timeline by EOD Monday (PST), I’ll coordinate internal stakeholders and Priya will gather security Qs.

Appreciate it —
Jordan
Product Lead, BrightLane

--
Attachment: initial-requirements.pdf (pdf)
From: mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com
To: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@brightlane.io>, priya.raman@brightlane.io
Cc: monica.patel@redwoodinference.com, neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — operational cadence and acceptance items

Jordan —

Thanks for the clear list. I’ve attached a working draft (BL_MAP_v0.3.xlsx) that maps milestones to owners, suggested gating criteria, and a 6-week pilot sprint calendar. High-level notes up front:

1) Pilot scope and dates
- Week 0 (prep): provisioning, sample data sync, security review
- Weeks 1–4 (pilot): staged traffic, weekly quality/latency reviews
- Week 5 (stabilize): full acceptance tests, load validation
- Week 6 (go/no-go): executive sign-off and cutover window

2) Owners and escalation path
- Redwood delivery lead: Mateo Alvarez (me) — overall MAP owner, weekly cadence
- Customer success (post-cutover): Monica Patel — onboarding deliverables and training
- Security & compliance liaison: Neha Kapoor — SOC/retention evidence and audit checklist

3) Acceptance criteria (examples)
- 99th percentile inference latency <= 300ms for targeted endpoints under pilot load
- No data persistence outside customer controlled buckets without documented consent
- Regression tests pass on the sample prompt set: accuracy threshold >= 92% (as measured by agreed eval harness)

4) Risks and mitigations
- Risk: KV cache warm-up may spike latency on day 1.
  Mitigation: staggered ramp + pre-warming with synthetic traffic (we outline steps in the sheet).

I also included a short security Q&A PDF that Priya asked for. Can you confirm whether BrightLane needs Redwood to run in a VPC during the pilot, or if hosted with IP allowlist is sufficient for initial testing? That determines provisioning lead times.

I’ll be available for a 30-minute sync tomorrow at 10am PT if that works for your team — booking link in the sheet.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0129

Attachments: BL_MAP_v0.3.xlsx (spreadsheet), security-qna-2026-08.pdf (pdf)
From: Priya Raman <priya.raman@brightlane.io>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com, monica.patel@redwoodinference.com, neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — operational cadence and acceptance items

Mateo / team —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the draft. A few clarifying items from Security/Product after a quick read:

- VPC vs hosted: Security prefers a short pilot in hosted + IP allowlist only if we can get audit logs (access + model invocation logs) for the pilot window. If audit logs are available, we can delay VPC until post-pilot. Can Redwood confirm log retention and export format?

- Acceptance metric: for the accuracy threshold you listed, can we see the eval harness and the seed prompt set you used? We want to mirror it in our internal tests.

- Rollback plan: please add a concrete rollback window and post-cutover monitoring checklist (alerts, runbook owner).

Also, Monica — would love your thoughts on training materials cadence (we were thinking two 1-hour sessions during week 4).

Happy to take the 10am PT slot if that’s still open — I’ll loop in our Ops lead if needed.

—Priya
Product Operations, BrightLane
From: mateo.alvarez@redwoodinference.com
To: Priya Raman <priya.raman@brightlane.io>, Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@brightlane.io>
Cc: monica.patel@redwoodinference.com, neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2026 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — operational cadence and acceptance items

Perfect — thanks for the questions. Quick answers and next steps:

- Logs: Redwood will expose invocation + access logs for the pilot. Retention: 90 days exportable as NDJSON or CSV. I added a Log Export checklist to tab 4 of the spreadsheet.

- Eval harness & prompts: Attached in the Drive link (tab 6). We’ll share the exact seed set and the evaluation script we ran for the 92% threshold so BrightLane can reproduce locally.

- Rollback & monitoring: Draft rollback window: first 48 hours after cutover; monitoring checklist and alert ownership added to the runbook (tab 5).

I updated the MAP sheet with these items and re-uploaded BL_MAP_v0.4 (same folder link). Monica — I penciled two 1-hour training sessions on Thu/Wed of week 4; please confirm if those times work and whether you want separate sessions for Engineering and Product.

If everyone is good, I’ll lock the MAP and send a calendar invite for the pilot kick-off meeting (provisioning checklist + acceptance review) tomorrow.

Cheers,
Mateo
